vintagecanvas:basics-text: Making paintings in Vintage Canvas Welcome to Vintage Canvas! To begin your creative journey, you'll need a couple of things at minimum: an easel, any shape of canvas, and a piece of charcoal. Place your easel in the world (ideally somewhere with good light). Place your canvas onto the easel using rightmousebutton. Then, hold your charcoal, and sketch away to your heart's content! Painting Once you're ready for a bigger challenge, it's time to create some paint! Make a couple of paint jars, fill them with oil, and add any pigment - like crushed lapis lazuli, cinnabar, charcoal - or one of the new pigments added by Vintage Canvas. Next, craft yourself one or all of the paint brushes. Right-click to dip your paint in the jar of your choice, and paint away! If you're looking for more than the flat colours of basic pigments, you have two options: paint thinning, and paint mixing. Paint Thinning To reduce the opacity of your paint, dip your brush with paint into a jar of turpentine. The more times you dip it, the more transparent the paint - ideal for making gradients and blended colours! Paint mixing Still not satisfied with the colours at your disposal? Time to craft a palette! When placed in the world, this nifty plank gives you nine slots in which to combine basic paints. Click any slot with a paint jar to add its colour to the mix. Keep adding paints until you've got your ideal tone! Right-click the slot with a brush to use the paint, same as any paint jar. To clean out a slot, right-click it with your turpentine jar. Large paintings To paint a large canvas, you need a large easel. Once you've got one set up, you can combine any two canvases into their corresponding upgraded size. You get four times the surface area for just twice the materials, so it's an excellent deal!
